problem:
Given that ${y}_{0}(x)=\operatorname{cos}⁡x$ is a particular solution of the Riccati differential equation

$$
{y}^{′}=2x\,{y}^{2}-4x\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,y+2x{cos}^{2}⁡x-\operatorname{sin}⁡x
$$

 

find the general solution of the equation.
worked_solution:
The equation

$$
{y}^{′}=2x\,{y}^{2}-4x\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,y+2x{cos}^{2}⁡x-\operatorname{sin}⁡x,
$$

is a Riccati differential equation of the form

$$
{y}^{′}=a(x){y}^{2}+b(x)y+c(x),
$$

where

$$
a(x)=2x,\,b(x)=-4x\operatorname{cos}⁡x,\,c(x)=2x{cos}^{2}⁡x-\operatorname{sin}⁡x.
$$

To reduce the given Riccati equation to a Bernoulli equation, we use the substitution

$$
y(x)=z(x)+{y}_{0}(x),
$$

where ${y}_{0}(x)$ is a known particular solution.
Differentiating gives

$$
{y}^{′}(x)={z}^{′}(x)+{y}_{0}^{′}(x).
$$

In our case, ${y}_{0}(x)=\operatorname{cos}⁡x.$ Since ${y}_{0}^{′}(x)=-\operatorname{sin}⁡x$, we have

$$
y=z+\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,⇒\,{y}^{′}={z}^{′}-\operatorname{sin}⁡x.
$$

Let's substitute these expressions into our Riccati equation:

$$
{z}^{′}-\operatorname{sin}⁡x=2x\,(z+\operatorname{cos}⁡x)^{2}-4x\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,(z+\operatorname{cos}⁡x)+2x{cos}^{2}⁡x-\operatorname{sin}⁡x.
$$

Now, we expand the right-hand side, and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}{z}^{′}-\operatorname{sin}⁡x & =2x({z}^{2}+2z\operatorname{cos}⁡x+{cos}^{2}⁡x)-4x\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,(z+\operatorname{cos}⁡x)+2x{cos}^{2}⁡x-\operatorname{sin}⁡x \\ {z}^{′}-\operatorname{sin}⁡x & =2x{z}^{2}-\operatorname{sin}⁡x \\ {z}^{′} & =2x{z}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

We can solve the obtained equation using separation of variables:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x} & =2x{z}^{2} \\ \frac{1}{{z}^{2}}\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x} & =2x \\ \int \frac{1}{{z}^{2}}\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x & =\int 2x\,\text{d}x \\ \int {z}^{-2}\,\text{d}z & =\int 2x\,\text{d}x \\ -\frac{1}{z} & ={x}^{2}+C \\ z & =-\frac{1}{{x}^{2}+C}\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is an arbitrary constant.

Finally, let's substitute $z=y-\operatorname{cos}⁡x$ to recover the initial variable $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}z & =-\frac{1}{{x}^{2}+C} \\ y-\operatorname{cos}⁡x & =-\frac{1}{{x}^{2}+C} \\ y & =-\frac{1}{{x}^{2}+C}+\operatorname{cos}⁡x \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡x-\frac{1}{{x}^{2}+C}\end{aligned}
$$
